# chroordinate

chroordinate allows you to coordinate chromosome coordinates during data
analysis.

## Installation

You can install the development version of chroordinate from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("joe-m-shaw/chroordinate")
```

## Naming convention

In `chroordinate` chromosomes are referred to as “chromosome” for
clarity, instead of “chr” (which can be mistaken for meaning
“character”) or “chrom”. For the second coordinate in a location,
`chroordinate` uses “end” not “stop”.

## Logo

The `chroordinate` logo uses an icon from FlatIcon made by
[Magnific](https://www.flaticon.com/free-icon/genetics_5685648?term=chromosome&related_id=5685648).

# Package index

## All functions

- [`extract_coordinates()`](https://joe-m-shaw.github.io/chroordinate/reference/extract_coordinates.md)
  : Extract genomic coordinates from a string
- [`factorise_chromosome()`](https://joe-m-shaw.github.io/chroordinate/reference/factorise_chromosome.md)
  : Convert human chromosomes into factors
- [`levels_chromosomes()`](https://joe-m-shaw.github.io/chroordinate/reference/levels_chromosomes.md)
  : Factor levels for human chromosomes
- [`mutate_coordinates()`](https://joe-m-shaw.github.io/chroordinate/reference/mutate_coordinates.md)
  : Add genomic coordinates in separate columns of a dataframe
